entities.name: Adalbert III of Bohemia
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Adalbert III of Bohemia (died 1200) was Archbishop of Salzburg from 1168 to 1177 and then from 1183 to 1200, one of the most important positions in the medieval German Church. His archiepiscopate was marked by conflict with Emperor Frederick Barbarossa over the Investiture-related questions that continued to trouble Church-empire relations decades after the Concordat of Worms (1122).

Salzburg was the metropolitan see of the entire Alpine region — its archbishop held authority over the dioceses of Bavaria, Austria, and parts of the Danube frontier — making it one of the most strategically important ecclesiastical positions in the Holy Roman Empire. Adalbert III's conflict with Barbarossa led to his deposition and exile for a period before he was restored to his see. His resistance to imperial pressure reflected the continuing significance of the Gregorian reform's principles.

His long archiepiscopate contributed to Salzburg's development as a centre of ecclesiastical culture and administration. The late twelfth century was a period of considerable activity in Salzburg's ecclesiastical architecture, administration, and intellectual life, and Adalbert III's patronage contributed to this development. His connections to the Bohemian dynasty through his family background gave him a distinctive position in the borderland between Bohemia and the Alpine Church.
